objective_summary: Clean, authoritative live proof of the same-run Quality-Engineer logic-failure route-back loop, closing the production gap run-20260917-logicrepair-002 discovered. The identical deterministic boundary regression was re-planted in demo-repo/src/loanflow/risk_bands.py (classify_dti and classify_ltv's LOW-boundary comparisons changed from '<=' to '<'). Discovery/Research/Implementation (first pass, classify_dti only) completed cleanly with real Architect and Engineer dispatches. A fresh Quality Engineer genuinely found AC-2 failing (classify_ltv, logic_bug) on its first real verification pass, correctly routed back (repair_attempt 1) to the same Engineer, which repaired classify_ltv with TDD-first evidence (C-3 failing, C-4 passing). The repair's implementation report was promoted through the NOW-FIXED live bridge to implementation-report.repair-1.json (the production fix for the run-002 gap, live-proven for the first time). The same Quality Engineer re-verified against it and genuinely passed both AC-1 and AC-2 (V-3, full 8-test suite, exit 0), promoted to verification-report.repair-1.json. The orchestrator independently re-confirmed with its own ORCH-1/ORCH-2 commands (both exit 0) and a clean git status/diff (demo-repo working tree byte-identical to HEAD). One dispatch-tooling anomaly occurred and was handled honestly: the FIRST Quality Engineer dispatch (a different agent identity) self-blocked with zero real verification work due to phantom '[handback-send-enforce]' messages unrelated to any protocol violation; this was retained as a continuity_broken event, not promoted as canonical evidence, and a genuinely fresh Quality Engineer instance completed the real verification work. final_verdict: pass, one genuine logic-bug repair cycle.
lessons_learned_appended: When dispatching a staged subagent (Engineer/Quality Engineer) via the Agent/SendMessage tooling, a background '[handback-send-enforce]' mechanism can inject forced-handback messages into the agent's own turn sequence before the orchestrator's real reply arrives, causing the agent to correctly self-block per its own bounded-rejection rule even though neither the orchestrator nor the agent violated the documented protocol. Treat a resulting self-blocked report with zero real command evidence as a continuity_broken event (not a product/verification verdict), retain it honestly, and dispatch a genuinely fresh agent instance for that phase rather than trying to resume or promote the phantom-caused blocked report as canonical.

Before designing a new mechanism for live_cli.py (the live orchestrator bridge), check whether harness/orchestrator/core.py's deterministic engine already solved the same problem -- it often has, since core.py is deterministically tested first and its own internal helpers (e.g. _validate_and_promote's filename override, driving the repair-round f'{stem}.repair-{n}.json' convention) can usually be extracted into a shared evidence_io.py function and reused by both, rather than inventing a parallel design. This closed the run-20260917-logicrepair-002 gap (FACT-20260918-PROMOTE-NO-REPAIR-PATH) cleanly: core.py already had the exact convention, live_cli.py just needed to expose it.
remaining_risks: A dispatch-tooling anomaly ('[handback-send-enforce]' phantom forced-handback messages) caused the first Quality Engineer dispatch to self-block with zero real work before a fresh dispatch succeeded -- this is a session/tooling-level quirk unrelated to the production fix, but not something this milestone's own code changes could prevent from recurring.
The ASSIGNMENT.md planted-flaky-test demonstration remains entirely separate and open -- this run addressed only the deterministic logic-bug half of that combined acceptance criterion.
follow_up_actions: Plan and execute the separate flaky-test infrastructure-flake demonstration milestone.
